name: Avatar
summary: Represents a person or an entity with a picture, or their initials when there is none.
description: An avatar shows who or what something belongs to: the author of a comment, the members of a project, a workspace. It displays a picture when there is one and the initials of the name otherwise, in a circle or a rounded square. Assistive technology reads it as an image named by the person, unless the name is written right next to it, in which case the avatar is decoration.

anatomy.description: Root: the disc or square, exposed as an image named by the person, or hidden when decorative. Carries the size and the shape.
The picture, covering the whole shape. Present when a source is given.
Up to two letters derived from the name, shown when there is no picture. Hidden from assistive technology: the container carries the full name.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Diameter of the avatar and size of the initials.

properties.name: Shape
properties.description: Circle for people, square for entities (workspaces, organizations).

options.description: A rounded square: organizations, projects, bots.

properties.name: Name
properties.description: Full name of the person or entity: the accessible name of the avatar, and the source of the initials.

properties.name: Picture
properties.description: Address of the picture. Without it the initials are shown.

properties.name: Decorative
properties.description: The name is written next to the avatar, so the avatar is hidden from assistive technology instead of repeating it.

states.description: The only state: an avatar has no interaction. A status or presence indicator would be another part, not specified here.

notes: A fixed square of the size, never stretched; the picture covers it; the initials are centered.
An avatar sits inline with the name or the item it identifies, aligned on the middle.

name.text: The avatar is an image named by the full name (aria-label on the container, which has role img); the picture inside has an empty alt and the initials are hidden, so the name is read once. A decorative avatar, next to the written name, is hidden entirely.

guidelines.text: An avatar is non-text content that identifies someone: it has a text alternative, the full name, as the accessible name of one image, whether it shows a picture or initials; that name is how the relationship to the content (its author, its owner) stays programmatic. Initials alone are not a name.

Render a span with role="img" and aria-label set to the name; the picture inside is an img with an empty alt (the span already carries the name) and the initials carry aria-hidden="true". The img role requires an accessible name.
When the name is written next to the avatar (a comment author, a member row), the avatar is pure decoration: hide it so the name is not read twice.
Initials contrast 7.34:1 (light) and 13.04:1 (dark) with the brand tint behind them; the picture is the person's and is not subject to a contrast requirement. The hairline border is decoration.
Nothing is conveyed by the avatar's color: the tint is the same for everyone.
Provide alternative text labels for custom interface images and icons so VoiceOver can describe them.
Describe each element: give the avatar the name as its content description, or null when the name is written next to it.

guidelines: The name is the full name as the person wrote it (Ada Lovelace), or the entity's name (Design team); the initials derive from its first and last words.
Never put a role or a status in the name; write them next to the avatar.

examples.name: Square, medium
examples.description: An entity rather than a person.

examples.name: Circle, medium, decorative
examples.description: The name is written next to the avatar, so the avatar is hidden.

decisions.text: Without a picture the avatar is the subtle brand fill with initials in the on-subtle brand text color, the same for everyone; a hairline in the level 1 edge color outlines every avatar.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library has no per-person palette; one tint avoids meaning by color.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the size scale, 24, 32 and 40 px (small, medium, large), with initials at 10, 12 and 14 px medium; two shapes, circle (default) and square with 4 px corners.
An avatar is one image named by the full name, or hidden when the name is written next to it; initials are never the accessible name.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions initials-on-brand-tint, sizes-and-shapes, named-image-or-decoration). A span exposed as an image named by the person, with a picture or initials; sizes small, medium, large; shapes circle and square; a decorative mode. Initials contrast 7.34 (light) / 13.04 (dark) on the brand tint.
